source_title: AlpinDale/foidfinder: Identify anime characters and series in images - GitHub
source_excerpt:
foidfinder names the characters and series in anime images. It runs PixAI Tagger v1.0 (Danbooru tags up to May 2026).
We have two compute backends at the moment:
The backend is chosen at runtime. The default, auto , uses MLX on Apple Silicon and CUDA when an NVIDIA GPU is visible.
Requires the NVIDIA Container Toolkit and a driver for CUDA 13.0 (580 or newer).
On first start the container downloads the int8 checkpoint alpindale/PixAI-v1.0-INT8 (0.6 GB) into the models volume. The kernels are compiled at build time for the CUDA_ARCHS build argument (default 8.9 , add 8.6 for RTX 30-series cards). Compose publishes its port on loopback only, so put a reverse proxy with TLS and rate limiting in front of it.
If the GPU host should not hold TLS or Cloudflare credentials, it can dial out to a proxy host over SSH instead of accepting connections. Its key can open one loopback port on the proxy and nothing else.
On the proxy, create a foidfinder-tunnel user with shell /usr/sbin/nologin , add the GPU host's public key to its authorized_keys with the prefix restrict,port-forwarding,permitlisten="127.0.0.1:18000",command="/usr/sbin/nologin" , and install deploy/sshd-tunnel.conf into /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/ . Add the site from deploy/Caddyfile and copy the built UI to /srv/foidfinder/webui .
On the GPU host, put the private key id_ed25519 and a known_hosts entry for the proxy in a directory. Set COMPOSE_FILE=compose.yaml:deploy/tunnel.compose.yaml , FOIDFINDER_TUNNEL_DESTINATION=foidfinder-tunnel@ and FOIDFINDER_TUNNEL_SECRETS= in .env , then run docker compose up -d .
The proxy sends the GPU host no client IPs, Cloudflare headers or cookies, and serves its responses as JSON under a sandboxing CSP. A compromised GPU host can return wrong tags but cannot serve pages on your domain. It does see the uploaded images.
foidfinder convert writes the int8 checkpoint for the CUDA backend, with config.json and a model card, ready for hf upload . The CUDA backend also loads the official checkpoint and quantizes it at startup, which takes longer and needs 3.3 GB of VRAM during loading instead of 0.9 GB. The MLX backend needs the official checkpoint.
Each option is set by an environment variable or the matching foidfinder serve flag.
Errors have the form {"error": {"code": ..., "message": ...}} .
Uploads are decoded in memory and never written to disk.
Both backends keep the 72×72 patch tokens in window order (3×3 windows of 24×24), so windowed attention needs no partition or merge transposes. The MLX backend matches the official implementation within 1e-5 in fp32 and 0.003 in fp16.
The CUDA backend quantizes every transformer GEMM to int8. Activations are rotated by a Hadamard matrix and scaled per token, and weights carry the same rotation and are scaled per output channel. Attention runs on fp16 tensor cores. Bias, RoPE, GELU and residual adds are fused into the GEMM epilogues, and each batch size runs as one CUDA graph. The GEMMs are limited by L2 bandwidth, so batching does not lower the time per image.
Agreement with the official fp32 model on 588 Danbooru posts from July to October 2026, at PixAI's thresholds (character 0.27, copyright 0.24). The top-1 column counts the 345 posts tagged with a character.
Apache-2.0. PixAI Tagger v1.0 is also Apache-2.0.
